topics.title: Flash clay calciner
topics.problem: Flash clay calciner: hold the degree of calcination above 94% at minimum energy without over-burning (inlet gas temperature and clay feed as inputs)
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: calcined clay, cement and concrete
topics.hook: Calcined clay can replace part of the clinker in cement, and the flash calciner is where that clay is made. Hot enough to activate the clay, cool enough not to ruin it.
topics.start: [Cantisani et al. 2024, dynamic modeling of a flash clay calciner, ADCHEM](https://www.arxiv.org/abs/2404.07674) (full equations, kinetics and parameter table); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: SISO PID from clay feed to calcination degree, as the authors suggest
topics.angle: learn a neural ODE or Koopman surrogate of the plug-flow DAE, run NMPC on it, then amortize into a policy; dynamics settle in seconds, so data is cheap

topics.title: Electric clay calcination plant
topics.problem: Electric flash-calcination plant: flexible operation under intermittent renewable power and prices
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: calcined clay, cement and concrete
topics.hook: An electrically heated calciner can run on clean power, if it learns to follow the price and availability of that power without missing its quality target.
topics.start: [Cantisani et al. 2025, electric flash clay calcination plant model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.11209v1); [steady-state process optimization, DYCOPS 2025](https://skoge.folk.ntnu.no/prost/proceedings/dycops-2025/DYCOPS2025_offline_program/contents/papers/0077.pdf); model rebuilt, public day-ahead prices
topics.baseline: Steady-state optimal operating curve plus PID on calcination degree
topics.angle: economic MPC with a decision-focused price forecaster, or a policy choosing plant load from price forecasts; reduce the plant model first

topics.title: Cement kiln pyro-process
topics.problem: Cement pyro-process (preheater, calciner, rotary kiln, cooler): free lime and specific heat consumption
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: calcined clay, cement and concrete
topics.hook: Most of cement's CO2 comes from making clinker, from the limestone itself and from the fuel. Shaving fuel per tonne while keeping clinker in spec matters at the scale of the whole industry.
topics.start: [Svensen et al. 2025, pyro-process simulation model](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.02886); [Svensen et al. 2024, rotary kiln model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.03200v1); [Svensen et al. 2026, PI pairing and tuning for the pyro-process](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.03489) (a ready-made baseline); model rebuilt
topics.baseline: Decentralized PI
topics.angle: linearized or learned model + MPC, or RL for setpoint supervision over the PI layer, the hierarchy industry uses; keep the grid coarse, dynamics take hours

topics.title: Alternative fuels in the precalciner
topics.problem: Precalciner temperature control with alternative-fuel co-firing and belt transport delays
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: calcined clay, cement and concrete
topics.hook: Waste-derived fuels displace coal, but their heating value drifts. A controller that estimates it on the fly lets a plant burn more of them safely.
topics.start: [Gallestey, ABB, advanced process control for alternative fuels in precalciners](https://library.e.abb.com/public/4ee4ca9cd1cd2ed0c1257b350030736a/Advanced%20Process%20Control%20to%20increase%20Alternative%20Fuels%20Usage%20in%20Cement%20Kilns_A4_cor.pdf); [Fernández Gassó et al. 2025, expert systems for kiln operation](https://riuma.uma.es/entities/publication/1852c959-889b-4d37-b7b6-62cec478c1b5); lumped model rebuilt
topics.baseline: PID with a Smith predictor and the expert rules
topics.angle: MPC with a learned calorific-value estimator, since slowly drifting fuel quality is the real problem; maximize the alternative-fuel share within the temperature, O2 and CO window

topics.title: Cement grinding circuit
topics.problem: Cement grinding circuit (ball mill and separator): kWh per tonne with fineness measured only hourly
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: calcined clay, cement and concrete
topics.hook: Grinding is one of a cement plant's biggest electricity users. The twist: product fineness is measured only once an hour.
topics.start: [Prasath et al. 2013, soft-constrained MPC of a cement grinding circuit, DYCOPS](https://skoge.folk.ntnu.no/prost/proceedings/dycops2013-and-cab2013/media/DYCOPS/files/0183.pdf) (full transfer-function model); [Huusom et al. 2005, first-principles grinding model, IFAC](https://skoge.folk.ntnu.no/prost/proceedings/ifac2005/Papers/Paper3670.html)
topics.baseline: Fuzzy or PID and the paper's soft MPC
topics.angle: identify the plant from closed-loop data, or offline RL with sparse delayed fineness labels; use the nonlinear plant with mismatch or it is too easy

topics.title: Cement plant as a flexible load
topics.problem: Cement plant as a flexible electrical load: mills and silos under day-ahead and intraday prices
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: calcined clay, cement and concrete
topics.hook: Mills and silos let a cement plant move its electricity use to hours when power is cheap and clean, which helps a grid full of wind and solar.
topics.start: [Rojas-Innocenti et al. 2024, electricity flexibility of industrial plants](https://arxiv.org/html/2411.09279v2); [robust scheduling for a cement plant with market participation, 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.10824); MILP fully specified
topics.baseline: Deterministic MILP with perfect foresight
topics.angle: decision-focused training of the price forecaster through the MILP, or an amortized policy on rolling horizons; pair with the grinding row for dynamics

topics.title: Low-carbon concrete mix design
topics.problem: Low-carbon concrete mix design as sequential experimental design (embodied carbon vs strength)
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: calcined clay, cement and concrete
topics.hook: Each tested mix takes 28 days to reveal its strength. Choosing which mixes to cast next is a sequential decision with a real carbon payoff.
topics.start: [Ament et al. 2023, sustainable concrete via Bayesian optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.18288); [BOxCrete, 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21525); [SustainableConcrete data and code](https://github.com/facebookresearch/SustainableConcrete)
topics.baseline: The Bayesian optimization loop in the repository
topics.angle: mix selection as a finite-horizon MDP, decision-focused strength model; not a dynamical system, so pair it with curing

topics.title: Precast steam curing
topics.problem: Precast steam-curing regime: energy vs early strength for 24-hour turnover
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: calcined clay, cement and concrete
topics.hook: Precast plants heat concrete with steam to free their moulds every day. A curing profile planned with a model can save much of that energy and still reach strength on time.
topics.start: [Lee et al. 2016, optimization of curing regimes for precast members](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40069-016-0154-7); [2023 follow-up with heat transfer and hydration](https://ascelibrary.com/doi/10.1061/JMCEE7.MTENG-15077); maturity model plus 1-D heat equation rebuilt
topics.baseline: Standard 3-6-3 regime and the paper's offline optimum
topics.angle: closed-loop MPC on measured member temperature, trajectory optimization with state constraints, robustness to ambient and mix variability

topics.title: Mass-concrete pipe cooling
topics.problem: Mass-concrete pipe cooling: hydration heat and cracking risk
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: calcined clay, cement and concrete
topics.hook: Thick pours heat up as cement hydrates and can crack as they cool. Chilled-water pipes are the actuator; the temperature-gradient constraint is the hard part.
topics.start: [Chen and Chen 2024, cooling-pipe control of mass concrete, Buildings](https://www2.mdpi.com/2075-5309/14/4/872); [Zhang et al. 2025, Shiziyang Bridge pile cap](https://jeas.springeropen.com/articles/10.1186/s44147-025-00685-x); 2-D heat model with hydration source rebuilt
topics.baseline: Fixed flow and inlet schedule
topics.angle: MPC with a learned reduced thermal model, cracking-risk penalty as a temperature-gradient proxy

topics.title: Carbonation curing of concrete blocks
topics.problem: Carbonation curing of precast blocks: maximize CO2 uptake and strength per cycle
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: calcined clay, cement and concrete
topics.hook: Curing blocks in CO2 instead of steam locks carbon into the concrete as minerals. Get the moisture and timing right and the blocks also come out stronger.
topics.start: [Shao et al. 2013, maximizing CO2 uptake in block carbonation, AIChE](https://proceedings.aiche.org/videos/maximizing-co2-uptake-concrete-blocks-carbonation); [Kashef-Haghighi 2012, McGill PhD thesis, 1-D reactive transport model](https://escholarship.mcgill.ca/downloads/d791sm26s); model rebuilt
topics.baseline: Fixed recipe
topics.angle: MPC on measured outlet CO2 with a learned uptake model; a Montreal angle (McGill, Quebec precast) may help with data

topics.title: 3D concrete printing
topics.problem: 3D concrete printing: closed-loop layer-width and buildability control
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: calcined clay, cement and concrete
topics.hook: Printing walls layer by layer saves material, but each layer must stiffen fast enough to carry the next. Speed against collapse is a clean control trade-off.
topics.start: [Shojaei Barjuei et al. 2022, vision-based layer-width control](https://doaj.org/article/6a6af1c1c47e4dc3a49f1742e7b67ad6); [Senthilnathan and Raphael 2024, buildability by computer vision, ISARC](https://www.iaarc.org/publications/fulltext/128_ISARC_2024_Paper_246.pdf); model rebuilt
topics.baseline: Open-loop G-code with the paper's PI width loop
topics.angle: rheology-aware learned dynamics + MPC on speed, pump rate and inter-layer delay

topics.title: Ready-mix concrete dispatch
topics.problem: Ready-mix concrete delivery dispatch on Quebec data, with carbon-weighted costs
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: calcined clay, cement and concrete
topics.hook: Concrete must be poured within a short window after batching. This one comes with 263 real days of orders from a Quebec producer.
topics.start: [Kinable et al. 2014, the concrete delivery problem, Computers and Operations Research](https://research.tue.nl/en/publications/the-concrete-delivery-problem/); [real operational data, 263 days from a Quebec producer](https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/b78bc94d95/1)
topics.baseline: MIP with perfect information as the hindsight bound
topics.angle: policy amortized from MILP solutions, RL for the intra-day dynamic version, decision-focused travel-time prediction

topics.title: Electric arc furnace heat
topics.problem: Electric arc furnace heat: hit tap temperature and carbon at minimum kWh per tonne
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: steel, aluminium, industrial heat, carbon removal and flexible chemicals
topics.hook: Arc furnaces make new steel from scrap with electricity instead of coal. Each heat is a short batch where every kWh and every degree of overshoot counts.
topics.start: [Coetzee et al. 2005, MPC of the refining stage of an EAF, IFAC](https://folk.ntnu.no/skoge/prost/proceedings/ifac2005/Fullpapers/04435.pdf) (5-state model); [Hay et al. 2019, EAF simulator, Processes](https://www.mdpi.com/2227-9717/7/11/852/htm); model rebuilt
topics.baseline: Operator power profile and PID electrode regulation
topics.angle: learned dynamics + MPC, robust MPC with a mid-heat temperature measurement

topics.title: Arc furnace scheduling under prices
topics.problem: EAF fleet scheduling under real-time electricity prices
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: steel, aluminium, industrial heat, carbon removal and flexible chemicals
topics.hook: A steel mill can move its biggest loads to cheap hours, if its schedule commits without knowing tomorrow's prices.
topics.start: [Pi et al. 2025, EAF scheduling under price volatility with RL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.09293); MILP fully specified, public NYISO prices
topics.baseline: Rule-based and hindsight MILP
topics.angle: amortized policy from MILP solutions, decision-focused price forecasting; non-anticipativity is the point

topics.title: Hydrogen direct-reduction furnace
topics.problem: Hydrogen direct-reduction shaft furnace as a flexible load
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: steel, aluminium, industrial heat, carbon removal and flexible chemicals
topics.hook: Reducing iron ore with hydrogen instead of coke could remove most of the CO2 from iron making. Running it on renewable power makes it a flexible-load problem.
topics.start: [Ji et al. 2026, demand response of a hydrogen metallurgy system](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.00379); [Hamadeh et al. 2018, shaft furnace model, Materials](https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1944/11/10/1865); model rebuilt
topics.baseline: Constant throughput and the deterministic MILP
topics.angle: MPC with learned shaft dynamics, RL for electrolyzer and furnace coordination under price uncertainty

topics.title: Slab reheating furnace
topics.problem: Continuous slab reheating furnace: nonlinear MPC of zone temperatures
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: steel, aluminium, industrial heat, carbon removal and flexible chemicals
topics.hook: Steel slabs are reheated in large gas-fired furnaces before rolling. The cited NMPC cut discharge temperature error from 13 K to under 1 K on a real plant; can a learned policy keep that at a fraction of the compute?
topics.start: [Steinboeck et al. 2013, NMPC of a slab reheating furnace, Control Engineering Practice](https://www.acin.tuwien.ac.at/fileadmin/cds/pre_post_print/steinboeck13a.pdf) (industrial results); model rebuilt
topics.baseline: Zone-based PI
topics.angle: amortize the NMPC into a policy, or learn the slab model from filtered logs and compare with the Galerkin model

topics.title: Aluminium smelter power modulation
topics.problem: Hall-Héroult aluminium cells: power modulation as virtual energy storage
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: steel, aluminium, industrial heat, carbon removal and flexible chemicals
topics.hook: Quebec's smelters run on hydro power. If the pots can swing their power without freezing or overheating, they become a giant battery for the grid.
topics.start: [Ma et al. 2023, MPC of cell superheat during power modulation, ICSOBA](https://icsoba.org/assets/files/publications/2023/Papers/AL54%20-%20Model%20Predictive%20Control%20of%20Maintaining%20the%20Superheat%20of%20an%20Aluminium%20Smelting%20Cell%20during%20Power%20Modulation.pdf); [Wong et al. 2025, power modulation of Hall-Héroult cells](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.07893); [Moreira et al. 2020, state-affine model from industrial pot data, IFAC](https://ifatwww.et.uni-magdeburg.de/ifac2020/media/pdfs/3368.pdf); model rebuilt
topics.baseline: Open-loop current step and the standard demand-feed logic
topics.angle: MPC with learned alumina-dissolution dynamics, two-timescale hierarchical control (cell minutes vs market hours); very relevant to Quebec

topics.title: Industrial heat pump with storage
topics.problem: Industrial heat pump with hot and cold thermal storage for batch processes
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: steel, aluminium, industrial heat, carbon removal and flexible chemicals
topics.hook: Heat pumps can supply much of the low-temperature heat factories now get from gas. With storage, a batch plant can reuse its own waste heat at the right moment.
topics.start: [Agner et al. 2024, MPC of heat pumps with thermal storage, Energies](https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1073/17/19/4823) (2-state model given); [Padullés et al. 2023, brewery case, ECOS](https://orbit.dtu.dk/en/publications/potential-for-optimal-operation-of-industrial-heat-pumps-with-the/)
topics.baseline: Rule-based charging and the MIQP MPC
topics.angle: decision-focused load and price forecasts through the MIQP, a learned policy handling the integer switching

topics.title: Firebrick thermal battery
topics.problem: Firebrick thermal battery dispatch for electrified process heat
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: steel, aluminium, industrial heat, carbon removal and flexible chemicals
topics.hook: Hot bricks store cheap renewable electricity as heat for factories, losing about one percent of it per day. The question is when to charge and when to hold back.
topics.start: [Jacobson et al. 2024, firebricks for industrial process heat, PNAS Nexus](https://web.stanford.edu/group/efmh/jacobson/Articles/Others/24-Firebricks.pdf) (unit parameters given); model rebuilt, public prices
topics.baseline: Priority heuristic and perfect-foresight LP
topics.angle: approximate DP under price uncertainty, multi-market bidding and demand uncertainty to make it hard

topics.title: Steel-plant waste-heat recovery
topics.problem: EAF off-gas waste-heat recovery: steam accumulator or packed bed smoothing a batch source
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: steel, aluminium, industrial heat, carbon removal and flexible chemicals
topics.hook: Off-gas from an arc furnace arrives in bursts; storage turns the bursts into steady steam. The disturbance is periodic, which a learned model can exploit.
topics.start: [Steinparzer et al. 2013, heat recovery steam generators at steelmaking](https://www.acin.tuwien.ac.at/fileadmin/acin/ijaa/ijaajg21h1.pdf); [Ortega-Fernández and Rodríguez-Aseguinolaza 2019, Applied Energy](https://scienceportal.tecnalia.com/en/publications/thermal-energy-storage-for-waste-heat-recovery-in-the-steelworks-/); lumped model rebuilt
topics.baseline: PID
topics.angle: MPC with a learned model of the periodic batch disturbance, RL for valve scheduling; lump the boiler or it eats the semester

topics.title: Glass melting furnace
topics.problem: Glass melting furnace: multivariable MPC on an identified model, electric boosting
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: steel, aluminium, industrial heat, carbon removal and flexible chemicals
topics.hook: Glass furnaces run for years at around 1500 °C. Shifting heat from gas burners to electric boosting while holding temperatures steady is a direct emissions lever.
topics.start: [Bacci di Capaci et al. 2024, model-based control of a glass melting furnace, ADCHEM](https://skoge.folk.ntnu.no/prost/proceedings/adchem-2024/files/0056.pdf); model rebuilt
topics.baseline: Decentralized PID
topics.angle: learned (Koopman or subspace) model + MPC, and how much data a learned model needs compared with N4SID

topics.title: Electric boiler and heat storage
topics.problem: Thermal storage with an electric boiler: classical advanced control vs coordinator MPC
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: steel, aluminium, industrial heat, carbon removal and flexible chemicals
topics.hook: A small, clean problem from Skogestad's group: can learning beat a well-designed classical control structure, or only match it?
topics.start: [Zotica et al. 2020, Skogestad group, HighEFF](https://sintef.no/globalassets/project/higheff/deliverables-2020/d1.2_2020.10-coordinator-mpc-for-thermal-energy-storage.pdf); single-tank model rebuilt
topics.baseline: Split-range and selector PID
topics.angle: RL or decision-focused forecasting against the coordinator MPC under forecast error; extend the network to several consumers

topics.title: Direct air capture cycles
topics.problem: Direct air capture: temperature-vacuum swing cycle control under varying weather
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: steel, aluminium, industrial heat, carbon removal and flexible chemicals
topics.hook: Sorbents pull CO2 straight out of the air, and how well they do it depends on the weather. A cycle that adapts to temperature and humidity lowers the cost per tonne removed.
topics.start: [Schellevis et al. 2024, optimizing DAC under varying weather, RSC](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlehtml/2024/ya/d4ya00200h); [Akinola and Wang 2026, multi-objective optimisation of solid-sorbent DAC](https://psecommunity.org/LAPSE:2026.0340v1); [pyDAC](https://github.com/process-intensification-lab/pyDAC)
topics.baseline: Fixed cycle from offline Pareto optimization
topics.angle: weather- and price-aware cycle scheduling with a learned surrogate; relevant to a cold climate

topics.title: Amine CO2 capture plant
topics.problem: Amine CO2 capture plant: capture-rate tracking and time-shifted solvent regeneration
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: steel, aluminium, industrial heat, carbon removal and flexible chemicals
topics.hook: Capture plants must follow a power plant that ramps with the grid. Regenerating solvent when steam is cheap is a storage problem hiding in a chemical plant.
topics.start: [Montañés et al. 2017, TCM amine plant model validation and control, Energies](https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1073/10/10/1527); [Jung and Lee 2022, NMPC with a learned surrogate, DYCOPS](https://skoge.folk.ntnu.no/prost/proceedings/dycops-2022/files/0124.pdf); [Åkesson et al. 2011, reduced absorber model](https://2011.international.conference.modelica.org/proceedings/pages/papers/03_3_ID_186_a_fv.pdf); plant-level view in [Wu et al. 2019, Int. J. Greenhouse Gas Control](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/id/eprint/146676/)
topics.baseline: Decentralized PID
topics.angle: learned surrogate + NMPC, economic MPC with a time-varying steam price; the reduced model is the realistic scope

topics.title: Biochar pyrolysis kiln
topics.problem: Biomass slow pyrolysis in a rotary kiln (biochar as carbon removal): yield and stability
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: steel, aluminium, industrial heat, carbon removal and flexible chemicals
topics.hook: Biochar locks plant carbon away for a long time and goes back into soils. The kiln decides how much of that carbon ends up stable.
topics.start: [Babler et al. 2017, slow pyrolysis in a rotary kiln, Applied Energy](https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/appene/v207y2017icp123-133.html); [Pichler et al. 2021 dataset](https://doaj.org/article/0192027231e446e4a73e503fb7325340) with [code](https://github.com/mptutvt/rotaryPyrolysis) and [13,851 simulated cases](https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/j3zm2xv53y/1)
topics.baseline: Fixed operating point
topics.angle: learned surrogate from the cases, add thermal inertia, MPC; the dynamic extension is your contribution and must be justified

topics.title: Flexible ammonia synthesis
topics.problem: Flexible Haber-Bosch: load-following of a quench-cooled ammonia reactor near its unstable region
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: steel, aluminium, industrial heat, carbon removal and flexible chemicals
topics.hook: Green ammonia needs reactors that follow wind and solar, yet the classic ammonia reactor can turn unstable at low load. Safe learning-based control meets a reactor that bites.
topics.start: [Rosbo et al. 2023, flexible operation of a quench-cooled ammonia reactor, Computers and Chemical Engineering](https://core.ac.uk/outputs/574387394); [Rosbo 2025, DTU PhD thesis](https://skoge.folk.ntnu.no/publications/thesis/2025_rosbo_dtu/DTU_PhD_Thesis_jwro.pdf); [Morud and Skogestad unstable reactor code](https://skoge.folk.ntnu.no/ammonia/control/)
topics.baseline: PID stabilization of the bed inlet temperature with RTO setpoints
topics.angle: NMPC on a learned reduced model, RL that must respect a stability constraint; use the 3-bed lumped model

topics.title: Power-to-methanol
topics.problem: Power-to-methanol: flexible synthesis vs intermediate storage under price variability
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: steel, aluminium, industrial heat, carbon removal and flexible chemicals
topics.hook: Should an e-fuel plant ramp with the price of power or buffer with storage? The answer decides much of what the fuel costs.
topics.start: [Mucci et al. 2023, cost-optimal power-to-methanol](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18338); model rebuilt
topics.baseline: Perfect-foresight schedule
topics.angle: rolling-horizon MPC with learned price forecasts; add a lumped reactor thermal state to make it a control problem

topics.title: Electrified methane reformer
topics.problem: Electrically heated steam methane reformer on a bench system
topics.section: Industrial decarbonization: steel, aluminium, industrial heat, carbon removal and flexible chemicals
topics.hook: Heating a reformer with electricity instead of burning gas removes the furnace's emissions. A real bench system with published parameters keeps the project honest.
topics.start: [Çıtmacı et al. 2024, MPC of an electrically heated SMR, Digital Chemical Engineering](https://doaj.org/article/a400bdc52d5940e89a89f4141e2428e6) (lumped model with experimental parameters)
topics.baseline: PI
topics.angle: learned dynamics + MPC with a tube-temperature constraint; small but real, so depth must come from the robustness study

topics.title: Sensor-driven waste bin collection
topics.problem: Each day, choose which sensor-equipped containers to empty and how to route a small truck fleet, given current fill levels and stochastic deposit rates, to minimize travel, handling and overflow penalty costs subject to truck capacity and shift length.
topics.hook: The paper's real case is Twente Milieu's 378-container network. There, tuning a simple bin-selection heuristic cut costs by up to about 40% against default settings, so choosing which bins to empty matters more than the routing. The Mildura file has about 42,000 ultrasonic distance-to-top readings for 7 bins from Dec 2021 to Sep 2023, enough to fit fill-rate and emptying-event models.
topics.start: [Mes, Schutten & Pérez Rivera 2013, Inventory routing for dynamic waste collection, BETA WP 431](https://ris.utwente.nl/ws/files/5141220/wp_431.pdf); [Markov et al. 2016, Inventory routing with non-stationary stochastic demands, EPFL report](https://infoscience.epfl.ch/record/221364); [Mildura smart-bin fill levels, data.gov.au (CC BY 3.0 AU)](https://data.gov.au/data/dataset/mildura-rrc-smart-bin-fill-levels/resource/b5e11aa0-6beb-4bd3-b164-20c4c01dc780); [City of Melbourne Netvox bin sensors, DataVic](https://discover.data.vic.gov.au/dataset/netvox-r718x-bin-sensor/resource/8aa57ce9-2939-4c70-92f7-c20e436fdd99); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: the paper's MustGo/MayGo threshold heuristic with cheapest insertion, or a fixed daily fraction of bins as in the operator's practice
topics.angle: ADP with a value function over fill levels for bin selection, with routing left to a heuristic; or amortize a rolling-horizon IRP solver into a fast selection policy

topics.title: Sorting-plant container emptying
topics.problem: Every 1 to 2 minutes, decide which of many continuously filling containers at the end of a waste sorting plant to send to a scarce processing unit, under stochastic fill rates, so containers are emptied near their ideal volume without ever overflowing.
topics.hook: The environment is derived from the final stage of a real waste sorting plant, and in the paper PPO, TRPO and DQN often lose to a naive rule-based controller. The fill dynamics are written out in the paper, so a model-based planner is a fair and easy-to-build challenger.
topics.start: [Pendyala et al. 2023, ContainerGym: A Real-World Reinforcement Learning Benchmark for Resource Allocation, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.02991); [ContainerGym code (MIT)](https://github.com/Pendu/ContainerGym); [Pendyala, Atamna & Glasmachers 2024, PPO with curriculum learning on the same sorting facility, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.02577)
topics.baseline: the paper's rule-based controller that empties the first container within one volume unit of its ideal emptying volume
topics.angle: MPC or rollout lookahead on the known random-walk-with-drift fill model and unit timers, compared with PPO/DQN

topics.title: Sorter throughput: purity vs yield
topics.problem: Set the feed rate (belt loading) of a sensor-based NIR/VIS sorter as input composition fluctuates, to maximize recovered target material while keeping product purity above a sales specification, with a buffer bunker limiting how far feed can be held back.
topics.hook: Küppers et al. found that yield falls exponentially with throughput while purity falls linearly with belt occupation density. The slope of the purity decline depends on input composition, so the best operating point moves with the feed. Friedrich et al. report that these response models must be fit per machine, even for the same material.
topics.start: [Küppers et al. 2020, Influence of throughput rate and input composition on sensor-based sorting efficiency, Detritus (open access)](https://digital.detritusjournal.com/articles/influence-of-throughput-rate-and-input-composition-on-sensor-based-sorting-efficiency/287); [Friedrich, Pomberger & Koinig 2024, Der optimale Betriebspunkt in der sensorgestützten Sortierung, Österr. Wasser- und Abfallwirtschaft (CC BY)](https://pureadmin.unileoben.ac.at/portal/files/26591658/s00506-023-01003-6.pdf); [Maus, Zengeler & Glasmachers 2025, SortingEnv: an RL environment for an industrial sorting process, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.10466); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: a fixed throughput setpoint chosen for nominal input composition
topics.angle: fit purity and yield response surfaces (GP) from the reported trials, then run chance-constrained MPC on feed rate and bunker level; or decision-focused learning of the response model

topics.title: Forced-aeration composting control
topics.problem: Over a 2 to 3 week batch, choose the aeration (and air heating) schedule of a forced-aeration pile to hold thermophilic temperature long enough for sanitization while keeping oxygen and moisture in range and minimizing fan energy, under uncertain substrate degradability and ambient conditions.
topics.hook: At the Colombian pilot plant the thermophilic phase stayed near 40 °C for about a week, below the 55 °C pathogen-elimination threshold, so aeration and heating are a real control problem. The 1996 model already includes fan operating costs, so energy enters the objective directly.
topics.start: [Stombaugh & Nokes 1996, Development of a biologically based aerobic composting simulation model, Trans. ASAE](https://uknowledge.uky.edu/bae_facpub/113/); [Patiño-Forero et al. 2025, Dynamic modeling of poultry litter composting in high mountain climates using system identification, Automation (open access)](https://www.mdpi.com/2673-4052/6/3/36/html); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: timer-based or on/off temperature-thermostat aeration at a fixed airflow
topics.angle: nonlinear MPC or trajectory optimization on the Monod, heat and moisture model; amortize it into a feedback policy and test robustness on the identified pilot-plant models

topics.title: Remanufacturing with sales-driven returns
topics.problem: Each period, decide how many returned cores to remanufacture and how many new units to produce, when buyback returns depend on sales from many past periods and demand is stochastic, to minimize production, holding and backlog costs over a finite horizon.
topics.hook: The case company's records cover 7 core types at two distribution centers from 2010 to 2014. In them, returns depend on sales from up to eight months earlier, so the state carries a long sales history and exact DP quickly becomes intractable. The paper's simple policy comes with a cost bound you can test a learned policy against.
topics.start: [Chou, Sim & Yuan 2020, Policies for inventory models with product returns forecast from past demands and past sales, Annals of Operations Research (open access)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10479-020-03545-4); [Inderfurth & van der Laan 2001, Leadtime effects and policy improvement for stochastic inventory control with remanufacturing, Int. J. Production Economics](https://repub.eur.nl/pub/14930); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: the paper's simplified feasible policy (cost gap bounded) or the four-parameter manufacture/remanufacture rule
topics.angle: ADP or policy gradient on the high-dimensional sales-history state, checked against exact DP on short-memory instances

topics.title: Grocery perishables ordering vs waste
topics.problem: Each day, choose order quantities for perishable grocery items given per-unit remaining shelf life in stock and uncertain demand, to maximize sales minus waste and missed sales.
topics.hook: RetaiL is fitted to item data from a large European grocer, released as copula-generated pseudo-items, and the authors report that classical supply-chain policies handle its uncertainty poorly. viso_jax gives exact optima for perishable problems with up to about 16 million states, so you can measure how far a learned policy is from optimal.
topics.start: [Jullien et al. 2023, A simulation environment and reinforcement learning method for waste reduction, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.15455); [RetaiL environment and GTDQN code](https://github.com/samijullien/GTDQN); [Farrington et al. 2023, GPU-accelerated value iteration and simulation for perishable inventory control using JAX, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.10672); [viso_jax code (Apache-2.0)](https://github.com/joefarrington/viso_jax)
topics.baseline: an (s, Q) ordering policy, or a base-stock policy tuned by simulation optimization
topics.angle: exact value iteration on small instances as ground truth, then distributional or offline RL and a single policy amortized across items with different shelf lives and margins

topics.title: Waste-to-energy grate combustion
topics.problem: Adjust ram feed, grate speed and primary/secondary air flows of a moving-grate incinerator to hold steam production and flue-gas O2 at setpoints, despite unmeasured swings in waste heating value and moisture, within combustion and emission limits.
topics.hook: Magnanelli et al. validated their Simulink model on plant data and found that raising waste humidity from 25% to 35% lengthened the steam-production response by 21 minutes. Leskens et al. note that the commercial controller holds only steam offset-free, which leaves O2 and economics on the table.
topics.start: [Magnanelli et al. 2020, Dynamic modeling of municipal solid waste incineration, Energy (open access)](https://www.sintef.no/en/publications/publication/1823541/); [Leskens et al. 2010, Improved economic operation of MSWC plants with a new model based PID control strategy, DYCOPS](https://skoge.folk.ntnu.no/prost/proceedings/dycops-2010/Papers_DYCOPS2010/WeMT4-03.pdf); [Ding, Tang & Qiao 2023, Dynamic modeling of multi-input and multi-output controlled object for MSWI, Applied Energy](https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/appene/v339y2023ics030626192300346x.html); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: a commercial PID combustion controller (offset-free on steam only) or the paper's model-based PID
topics.angle: offset-free MPC with an estimator for waste heating value and moisture, or a learned dynamics model plus MPC, on a simulator rebuilt from the mass and energy balances

topics.title: Scrap charge mix under composition drift
topics.problem: For each furnace heat, choose the masses of each scrap grade (and virgin iron) to meet Cu and Ni specifications at minimum cost, when scrap compositions are uncertain, drift over time and are only seen afterwards through the steel analysis.
topics.hook: Cu and Ni do not go to the slag, so uncertainty in scrap composition directly caps how much scrap a heat can take. On the paper's synthetic benchmark (45 scrap types, 20,000 heats), a Kalman filter cut Cu estimation error to 13.25 ppm from 16.93 ppm for windowed least squares.
topics.start: [Zhou, Naert & Nuyens 2025, Modeling scrap composition in electric arc and basic oxygen furnaces, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.09382); [Gaustad et al. 2016, Operational strategies for increasing secondary materials in metals production under uncertainty, J. Sustainable Metallurgy](https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/109890); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: deterministic LP blending on windowed least-squares composition estimates, or a chance-constrained blend with normal approximations
topics.angle: Kalman-filter belief state plus chance-constrained MPC over the next heats; decision-focused learning of composition estimates; value of exploring poorly known grades

topics.title: District heating network
topics.problem: District heating network: supply-temperature setpoint and thermal-storage dispatch with pipe transport delays
topics.section: Climate: heat, cold, shipping and generation
topics.hook: Hot water takes time to travel through city pipes, so the plant must act before the cold arrives. Delays plus storage make this a textbook MPC problem.
topics.start: [Deng et al. 2023, deep RL for fuel cost in district heating, Sustainable Cities and Society](https://research.abo.fi/fi/publications/deep-reinforcement-learning-for-fuel-cost-optimization-in-distric); [Le Coz et al. 2020, NeurIPS Climate Change AI workshop](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.09508); [pandapipes](https://github.com/e2nIEE/pandapipes)
topics.baseline: Operator heating curve
topics.angle: learned RC or RNN dynamics + MPC, offline RL on operation logs, policy amortized from MILP dispatch

topics.title: Fifth-generation district heating
topics.problem: Fifth-generation district heating and cooling with seasonal ice storage
topics.section: Climate: heat, cold, shipping and generation
topics.hook: A neighbourhood network near ground temperature, with an ice tank that freezes in winter and cools buildings in summer. Seasonal MPC on a field-validated model.
topics.start: [Kollmar et al. 2025, Applied Energy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.18528v1), field-validated; open [Modelica model](https://github.com/hka-esa/n5GDHC_sim)
topics.baseline: PI on the mixing valve tracking seasonal references
topics.angle: surrogate dynamics from the Modelica model + economic MPC over a seasonal horizon

topics.title: Heat-pump water heater
topics.problem: Heat-pump water heater as a thermal battery under price signals
topics.section: Climate: heat, cold, shipping and generation
topics.hook: Millions of hot-water tanks could act as a distributed battery. A classic fitted Q iteration application, now with a well-documented simulator.
topics.start: [Ruelens et al. 2015, RL applied to an electric water heater](https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.00408) (40-day lab experiment); [NREL OCHRE](https://github.com/NREL/OCHRE) stratified-tank model
topics.baseline: Thermostat
topics.angle: batch RL from logs, learned tank model + MPC, MILP schedule amortized into a policy

topics.title: Heat-pump defrost
topics.problem: Air-source heat-pump defrost initiation as optimal stopping
topics.section: Climate: heat, cold, shipping and generation
topics.hook: In a cold climate, frost on the outdoor coil quietly eats heat-pump efficiency. Deciding when to defrost is optimal stopping with a hidden state.
topics.start: [Klingebiel et al. 2025, self-optimizing defrost initiation, Applied Energy](https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/appene/v398y2025ics0306261925011304.html); frost-growth model rebuilt from the literature
topics.baseline: Manufacturer time or temperature-difference threshold
topics.angle: DP optimal stopping on a frost-growth model vs RL; maximize seasonal COP

topics.title: Heat-pump fleet flexibility
topics.problem: Residential heat-pump fleet as a flexibility aggregator under a feeder limit
topics.section: Climate: heat, cold, shipping and generation
topics.hook: Quebec's winter peak is driven by heating. Coordinating many heat pumps under a feeder limit without anyone getting cold is what utilities want.
topics.start: [Nespoli and Medici 2025, forecasting residential flexibility](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/energy-research/articles/10.3389/fenrg.2025.1547617/pdf); [Chen et al. 2020, distributed control of thermostatic loads](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.00791); [i4b simulator](https://github.com/lfrison/i4b) ([Zhang et al. 2024, constrained RL for safe heat-pump control](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19716v1))
topics.baseline: Heating curve per building
topics.angle: aggregate surrogate + MPC, decision-focused training of the flexibility forecaster, constrained RL

topics.title: Supermarket CO2 refrigeration
topics.problem: Supermarket transcritical CO2 refrigeration: control and price-driven load shifting
topics.section: Climate: heat, cold, shipping and generation
topics.hook: Supermarkets are switching to CO2 as a refrigerant to avoid potent synthetic gases. The food on the shelves doubles as thermal storage for load shifting.
topics.start: [Mazare et al. 2026, data-driven predictive control for CO2 refrigeration, Int. J. Refrigeration](https://vbn.aau.dk/en/publications/optimal-data-driven-predictive-control-for-transcritical-co2-refr/); [Hovgaard et al. 2012, economic MPC for refrigeration, Energy](https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/energy/v44y2012i1p105-116.html); model from [Shafiei et al. 2013, Energies](https://ideas.repec.org/a/gam/jeners/v6y2013i2p900-920d23546.html)
topics.baseline: PID or hysteresis per display case
topics.angle: data-driven predictive control vs learned-model MPC, goods as thermal storage

topics.title: Cold-storage warehouse
topics.problem: Cold-storage warehouse as thermal storage for demand response
topics.section: Climate: heat, cold, shipping and generation
topics.hook: A frozen-food warehouse can switch off for hours without harm. How long and when, given prices and door openings, is a clean economic MPC problem.
topics.start: [Mammoli et al. 2022, eceee Summer Study](https://www.eceee.org/library/conference_proceedings/eceee_Summer_Studies/2022/9-deep-decarbonisation-of-industry/demand-response-capabilities-of-industrial-refrigerated-warehouses-experiences-in-practical-implementation/); lumped thermal model rebuilt
topics.baseline: Fixed setpoint
topics.angle: economic MPC with price forecasts, offline RL; needs stochastic door and infiltration loads to be non-trivial

topics.title: Ship weather routing
topics.problem: Least-CO2 ship weather routing under forecast uncertainty
topics.section: Climate: heat, cold, shipping and generation
topics.hook: Ships carry most of world trade on heavy fuel. Routing around weather is one of the few emission cuts available to a ship already at sea.
topics.start: [VISIR-2, Mannarini et al. 2024, Geoscientific Model Development](https://gmd.copernicus.org/articles/17/4355/2024/) with [code](https://zenodo.org/records/15497175); [Bora et al. 2026, physics-informed offline RL for maritime routing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17319); [NOAA AIS data](https://coast.noaa.gov/digitalcoast/data/vesseltraffic.html)
topics.baseline: Great circle and the VISIR graph search
topics.angle: MPC on forecast ensembles, offline RL from AIS logs, amortized routing policy

topics.title: Rotor sails on cargo ships
topics.problem: Rotor-sail (Flettner) rpm control in cooperation with the engine
topics.section: Climate: heat, cold, shipping and generation
topics.hook: Spinning rotor sails turn wind into thrust on cargo ships. Their rpm has to be coordinated with the engine as the wind shifts.
topics.start: [Tillig and Ringsberg 2020, wind-assisted cargo ships, Ocean Engineering](https://research.chalmers.se/publication/517710); [Jang et al. 2026, fixed vs adaptive rotor speed control, J. Marine Science and Engineering](https://mdpi-res.com/d_attachment/jmse/jmse-14-00210/article_deploy/jmse-14-00210.pdf); ship model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: Fixed rpm and the paper's rule-based controller
topics.angle: MPC over the wind forecast, learned aerodynamic model

topics.title: Just-in-time port arrival
topics.problem: Just-in-time port arrival: speed profile under berth uncertainty
topics.section: Climate: heat, cold, shipping and generation
topics.hook: Ships often sprint to port and then wait at anchor. Slowing down to arrive when the berth frees up saves fuel, if you can reason about when it will.
topics.start: [Jia et al. 2017, virtual arrival policy, Transportation Research Part D](https://www.nhh.no/en/research-centres/shipping-and-logistics/news/2017/new-article-by-adland-and-jia/) (5,066 voyages from AIS); NOAA AIS
topics.baseline: Full speed then wait
topics.angle: stochastic DP over berth availability, MPC on the speed profile with a cubic fuel law

topics.title: Concentrated solar power
topics.problem: Concentrated solar power tower: receiver and cycle start-stop with storage dispatch
topics.section: Climate: heat, cold, shipping and generation
topics.hook: A molten-salt tower stores sunlight as heat and sells power after sunset. Start-ups are costly, so dispatch is a mixed-integer problem worth amortizing.
topics.start: [Wagner et al. 2017, optimized dispatch in a CSP production model, Applied Energy](https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/appene/v203y2017icp959-971.html); [NREL SAM simulation core](https://github.com/NREL/ssc)
topics.baseline: Heuristic dispatch and the rolling MILP
topics.angle: amortize the MILP into a policy, decision-focused irradiance and price forecasting

topics.title: Solar tracker control
topics.problem: Bifacial single-axis PV tracker angle control with backtracking
topics.section: Climate: heat, cold, shipping and generation
topics.hook: Trackers already follow the sun, but with two-sided panels and passing clouds the best angle is not obvious. Small gains on very large fleets add up.
topics.start: [Tsuchida et al. 2022, deep RL for bifacial tracker control, Energies](https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1073/15/21/8083/htm); [pvlib](https://github.com/pvlib/pvlib-python)
topics.baseline: Astronomical tracking with backtracking
topics.angle: MPC with an irradiance nowcast; gains are a few percent, so evaluation must be careful

topics.title: Nuclear microreactor load following
topics.problem: Nuclear microreactor load following with control drums
topics.section: Climate: heat, cold, shipping and generation
topics.hook: Small reactors could back up a renewable grid if they follow load smoothly. Point kinetics, temperature feedback and xenon make a rich nonlinear control problem.
topics.start: [Tunkle et al. 2025, microreactor control with deep RL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.00156) (point kinetics, temperature feedback, xenon, all equations given); [Dupré and Grossetête 2026, MPC for flexible PWR operation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20169)
topics.baseline: PID
topics.angle: NMPC on point kinetics, Koopman or linearized MPC, xenon-aware long-horizon planning

topics.title: Run-of-river hydro cascade
topics.problem: Run-of-river hydropower cascade: level control and schedule tracking
topics.section: Climate: heat, cold, shipping and generation
topics.hook: Plants in a chain share one river, so every release travels downstream. On the cited digital twin, RL still loses to human dispatchers: a fair target.
topics.start: [Vytvytskyi et al. 2015, Modeling, Identification and Control](https://www.mic-journal.no/ABS/MIC-2015-4-4.asp); [Rot Weiss et al. 2025, cascade dispatch with deep RL on a digital twin, Energies](https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1073/18/17/4660) (RL still loses to human dispatchers, a good target); [Santosuosso and Wogrin 2025, stochastic MPC](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11998)
topics.baseline: PI level control and human dispatch
topics.angle: learned linear or Koopman model + MPC

topics.title: Biomass furnace emissions
topics.problem: Biomass grate furnace: emission-limited MPC
topics.section: Climate: heat, cold, shipping and generation
topics.hook: Small biomass boilers emit carbon monoxide and particles when poorly controlled. The cited MPC cut CO several-fold; learn the model and keep the gain.
topics.start: [Böhler et al. 2021, emission-limited MPC of a biomass furnace, Applied Energy](https://repositum.tuwien.at/handle/20.500.12708/20504); zone model from [Boriouchkine and Jämsä-Jounela 2016, Energies](https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1073/9/9/735/html)
topics.baseline: Static feedforward + PI
topics.angle: grey-box identification + MPC with CO and O2 constraints

topics.title: Industrial thermoacoustic heat pump drive
topics.problem: Electrically driven thermoacoustic heat pump lifting industrial waste heat above 100 °C: set the drive ratio and frequency to deliver the required heat at the best COP while keeping motor power and temperature within limits near acoustic resonance
topics.hook: In tests the ECN prototype pumped heat from about 41 °C to 109 °C with an internal COP of about 4.8, but its drive motor overheated near acoustic resonance, which forced a 3.49% drive ratio instead of the 5% design value.
topics.start: [Tijani et al. 2017, development of a thermoacoustic heat pump for distillation column, IEA Heat Pump Conf.](https://publications.tno.nl/publication/34631718/r10Ya6/m16072.pdf); [Tijani et al. 2014, bench-scale electrically driven thermoacoustic heat pump (design)](https://publications.tno.nl/publication/34631561/i17Fz0/m14025.pdf); [DeltaEC, free LANL thermoacoustics code](https://lanl.gov/org/ddste/aldps/materials-physics-applications/quantum/thermoacoustics/computer-codes.php); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: fixed drive frequency and a hand-set drive ratio kept below the motor's thermal limit, as in the ECN tests
topics.angle: calibrate a Rott/DeltaEC model to the reported operating point, then MPC or iLQR on drive amplitude and frequency with a motor-heating constraint; takes the course book's synthetic thermoacoustic iLQR demo to a published device

topics.title: Two-source compact thermoacoustic heat pump
topics.problem: Compact thermoacoustic heat pump driven by two acoustic sources: set the source amplitudes and their relative phase to pump a target heat load at the least acoustic power
topics.hook: TACOT aims at a compact thermoacoustic cooler for cars. In the 2D model the best pressure-velocity phase lies between 5π/6 and π, while linear theory puts it at 3π/4, so a controller tuned on the cheap model chooses the wrong operating point.
topics.start: [Fraigneau, Weisman, Baltean-Carlès 2023, numerical model of thermoacoustic heat pumping inside a compact cavity, Acta Acustica](https://acta-acustica.edpsciences.org/10.1051/aacus/2023008); [TACOT project description (ANR)](https://anr.fr/Project-ANR-17-CE06-0007); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: fixed phase and amplitude chosen from linear-theory design
topics.angle: fit a cheap linear-theory model, then learn its correction from higher-fidelity runs so the chosen phase is right where it matters (decision-focused calibration), and optimize the drive

topics.title: Elastocaloric regenerator cycle
topics.problem: Elastocaloric regenerator: time the loading, unloading and fluid flow to maximize cooling per unit of work under a fatigue-limiting strain bound
topics.hook: The Ljubljana NiTi regenerator reached a 31.3 K span and over 60 W (4,400 W/kg at a 10 K span). The 1D model, validated against experiments and written in MATLAB, uses step flow and instantaneous loading, so shaping the cycle is left open.
topics.start: [Ahčin et al. 2022, numerical modeling of a shell-and-tube-like elastocaloric regenerator, Energies](https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1073/15/23/9253); [Ahčin et al. 2022, fatigue-resistant elastocaloric cooling and heat pumping in compression, Joule (lab page)](https://lahde.fs.uni-lj.si/en/high-performance-cooling-and-heat-pumping-based-on-fatigue-resistant-elastocaloric-effect-in-compression/); [Qian et al. 2023, multimode elastocaloric cooling system, Science (summary)](https://ceee.umd.edu/news/story/elastocaloric-cooling-system-codeveloped-by-ceee-faculty-featured-innbspscience); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: fixed Brayton-like cycle with step on/off flow at a swept frequency
topics.angle: periodic trajectory optimization of the strain and flow waveforms on the 1D model, amortized into a policy over span and load; optionally learn when to switch between regeneration and maximum-utilization modes as in the Maryland device

topics.title: Magnetocaloric heat pump seasonal operation
topics.problem: Magnetocaloric heat pump for a house: choose cycle frequency, fluid flow rate and the number of active regenerators each hour to meet heating demand at the highest seasonal COP
topics.hook: The open Python model takes flow and field profiles over the cycle as inputs. The paper reaches a seasonal COP of 5.6 by adjusting flow and frequency and switching regenerator groups, and estimates about 69 regenerators for peak demand, which leaves room to test a predictive policy against it.
topics.start: [Pineda Quijano et al. 2024, seasonal COP of a residential magnetocaloric heat pump based on MnFePSi, Int. J. Refrig.](https://iifiir.org/en/fridoc/seasonal-cop-of-a-residential-magnetocaloric-heat-pump-based-on-mnfepsi-148745); [Pineda Quijano et al. 2023, layering strategies for AMRs, Appl. Therm. Eng. (open access)](https://research.tudelft.nl/en/publications/layering-strategies-for-active-magnetocaloric-regenerators-using-); [code: FAME_AMR_model, Python 1D AMR](https://github.com/diego-pineda/FAME_AMR_model); [data and code, 4TU](https://data.4tu.nl/datasets/cd51b1e3-ab4a-4e6c-a668-f53da25475d4)
topics.baseline: the paper's strategy: set flow and frequency from steady-state maps and switch regenerator groups on and off to match demand
topics.angle: train a fast surrogate of the 1D AMR model, then MPC or DP over hourly demand using the building's thermal mass

topics.title: Adsorption chiller cycle timing
topics.problem: Two-bed adsorption chiller on solar or waste heat: choose the adsorption, desorption and mass-recovery phase durations as source and ambient temperatures drift, to trade cooling power against COP
topics.hook: On a validated Modelica model of a test bed, cutting the cycle from 1860 s to about 393 s raised volumetric cooling power from 29 to 42 kW/m3 for silica gel but lowered COP substantially, so the best timing depends on what the heat source can supply.
topics.start: [RWTH (Bardow group) 2015, optimal design of adsorption chillers based on a validated dynamic object-oriented model, Sci. Technol. Built Environ. (open manuscript)](https://publications.rwth-aachen.de/record/466219/files/466219.pdf); [Gräber et al. 2011, optimal cyclic operation of two-bed adsorption chillers with mass recovery](https://iifiir.org/en/fridoc/optimal-cyclic-operation-of-two-bed-adsorption-chillers-with-mass-27649); [Daborer-Prado and Resch 2021, lumped two-bed silica gel/water chiller model](https://pure.fh-ooe.at/en/publications/preliminary-results-on-experimental-modelling-of-an-adsorption-ch/); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: fixed cycle time tuned offline at nominal temperatures
topics.angle: periodic optimal control by multiple shooting, amortized into a feedback policy of heat-source and ambient temperature; compare with MPC over a varying heat source

topics.title: Absorption heat pump part-load control
topics.problem: LiBr/H2O absorption heat pump or chiller: modulate the driving heat and the internal and external flows to track output temperature over a wide part-load range
topics.hook: Absorption devices run on heat instead of electricity, but Staudt et al. note that poor control limits their modulation and part-load range. They provide a validated control-oriented model and a linearized state-space version intended for MPC.
topics.start: [Staudt et al. 2023, control-oriented modeling of a LiBr/H2O absorption heat pumping device with experimental validation, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.15097); [code: Absolut Modelica library for absorption cycles](https://github.com/carlesRT/Absolut)
topics.baseline: conventional PI control of output temperature
topics.angle: linear or nonlinear MPC on the validated DAE model, with a learned residual fitted on Modelica runs

topics.title: Variable-geometry ejector chiller
topics.problem: Heat-driven ejector chiller with a movable spindle: set the primary-nozzle area ratio as generator and condenser conditions vary, to maximize COP while keeping the ejector in critical mode
topics.hook: In the R290 study, moving the spindle raised the entrainment ratio by about 86% but lowered the critical pressure by about 283 kPa, so the best position depends on the condenser condition. That makes it a feedback problem, not a design choice.
topics.start: [Besagni and Inzoli 2022, influence of variable geometry control on an R290 ejector refrigeration system, J. Phys. Conf. Ser.](https://re.public.polimi.it/retrieve/e0c31c12-dbfe-4599-e053-1705fe0aef77/Besagni_2022_J._Phys.__Conf._Ser._2177_012010.pdf); [code: simpy_ejector, 1D ejector simulator (CoolProp)](https://github.com/AdamBuruzs/simpy_ejector); cycle model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: fixed-geometry ejector, or the spindle look-up table the authors propose
topics.angle: wrap simpy_ejector in a lumped cycle model, amortize the spindle optimization into a policy of measured temperatures, and use MPC when the generator's thermal inertia matters

topics.title: 150 °C steam heat pump start-up and turndown
topics.problem: Cascade heat pump making 150 °C steam from an ambient source: coordinate compressor speeds and expansion-valve superheat setpoints through cold start and load changes, avoiding liquid at compressor inlets and staying inside compressor maps
topics.hook: Steam heat pumps like this cascade prototype (R1233zd(E) over R513a) are meant to replace fossil steam boilers. The thesis shows that the plain PID scheme needs an ad hoc superheat change during turndown to keep liquid out of the compressors.
topics.start: [Ryan 2024, transient modeling of an ambient-source centrifugal-compressor steam-generating heat pump, Colorado State MS thesis](https://mountainscholar.org/items/81dbe058-fd5b-499b-b3ee-e9454baa2c59/full); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: PID loops with a fixed LP/HP compressor speed ratio and a temporary 15 K superheat setpoint during turndown
topics.angle: constrained MPC on a reduced cascade model that coordinates the three compressors and both valves, with a learned surrogate for the heat exchangers

topics.title: Electrified milk evaporator (MVR)
topics.problem: Falling-film milk evaporator with mechanical vapor recompression: set the compression ratio and feed temperature over time to reach the target dry-mass content at the least electricity cost
topics.hook: MVR is a heat pump that replaces process steam with electricity. In this model, dynamic optimization cut the annual electricity cost by about 30% for a 35% dry-mass product, and the authors find the case for MVR is sensitive to the electricity price.
topics.start: [Tsochatzidi, Arvanitidis, Georgiadis 2024, model-based optimization of energy consumption in milk evaporators, Processes](https://mdpi-res.com/d_attachment/processes/processes-12-00209/article_deploy/processes-12-00209.pdf); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: steady operation at a fixed compression ratio and feed temperature (the paper's non-optimized case)
topics.angle: economic MPC on the evaporator model with time-varying electricity prices and dry-mass constraints, then amortize the dynamic optimization into a policy

topics.title: Vapor-compression superheat benchmark
topics.problem: Single-stage vapor-compression chiller: move compressor speed and expansion-valve opening to track the brine outlet temperature and evaporator superheat under inlet-temperature disturbances
topics.hook: The Simulink benchmark comes with fixed 20-minute test scenarios, input constraints and a combined score, so a student can compare a learned or predictive controller with tuned PID in a week. Its refrigerant is R404a, which makes moving the model to a low-GWP refrigerant a natural extension.
topics.start: [Bejarano et al. 2018, benchmark for PID control of refrigeration systems based on vapour compression, IFAC PID'18](https://skoge.folk.ntnu.no/prost/proceedings/PID-2018/0043.PDF); [code: MATLAB/Simulink benchmark files](https://www.dia.uned.es/~fmorilla/benchmarkPID2018/)
topics.baseline: the benchmark's default decentralised PID controller
topics.angle: linear or nonlinear MPC, or an RL policy trained in the simulator, scored with the benchmark's combined index J; extension: rebuild the moving-boundary model for propane or CO2

topics.title: Field heat pumps: weather-curve tuning
topics.problem: Installed air-source heat pumps: choose each home's weather-compensation curve (slope and offset) from its own monitoring data to maximize seasonal performance without losing comfort or causing short cycling
topics.hook: OpenEnergyMonitor's analysis of the EoH trial finds a mean SPF H4 of 2.81 across 428 air-source units, against 3.86 for 170 HeatpumpMonitor systems, and links much of the gap to weather-compensation curves set too high.
topics.start: [Electrification of Heat heat pump performance cleansed data 2020-2023, UK Data Service SN 9050 (open, OGL)](https://b2find.eudat.eu/dataset/21e967cf-72a2-5344-b412-3e8e14cc1afb); [OpenEnergyMonitor analysis of the EoH trial data](https://docs.openenergymonitor.org/heatpumpmonitor/eoh.html); [worked examples of curves set too high](https://docs.openenergymonitor.org/heatpumpmonitor/commissioning.html); model learned from the data
topics.baseline: the installer's or factory-default weather-compensation curve
topics.angle: fit a per-home grey-box model (building, COP and cycling) from the monitoring data, then optimize the curve offline; compare a model fitted for prediction with one fitted for the decision

topics.title: Heat pump inspection targeting (HEAPO)
topics.problem: Heat pump optimization visits: decide which households to inspect and which settings to change, using smart-meter data and past inspection outcomes, to maximize the electricity saved per visit
topics.hook: Of 410 consultant reports, 168 (41%) flagged a heating curve set too high. The dataset pairs those visits with 15-minute smart-meter data from 1,408 Zurich households from 2018 to 2024, enough to test whether a learned targeting rule would have chosen the right homes.
topics.start: [Brudermueller et al. 2025, HEAPO open dataset for heat pump optimization, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.16993); [data, Zenodo (CC BY 4.0)](https://zenodo.org/records/15056919); [code: Python data loader](https://github.com/tbrumue/heapo)
topics.baseline: the consultants' visits as actually scheduled, plus the rule of thumb that the heating curve is usually too high
topics.angle: estimate per-household intervention effects from smart-meter data before and after visits, then learn a targeting policy offline and evaluate it with off-policy estimators

topics.title: Boreal forest management
topics.problem: Boreal forest management: carbon storage vs permafrost thaw over 50 years
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: Boreal forests hold huge carbon stocks above permafrost. Thinning and species choices trade carbon today against thaw tomorrow.
topics.start: [BoreaRL, Dsouza et al., ICLR 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.19846); [code](https://github.com/kevinbdsouza/BoreaRL)
topics.baseline: No management or a fixed thinning rule
topics.angle: DP or model-based RL with a learned surrogate of the physics simulator

topics.title: Peatland water tables
topics.problem: Peatland water-table control for greenhouse-gas mitigation
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: Drained peat releases its carbon as it dries out; keeping it wet stops much of that. A Nature paper gives the emission curve to control against.
topics.start: [Evans et al. 2021, water table control on peatland emissions, Nature](https://nora.nerc.ac.uk/id/eprint/530414/); [Mahmoodi et al. 2026, HESS](https://hess.copernicus.org/articles/30/6019/2026/hess-30-6019-2026.html) with field data
topics.baseline: Fixed weir setting
topics.angle: learned hydrology + MPC with rainfall forecasts; the emission relation is an annual mean, treat it with care

topics.title: Rice paddy wetting and drying
topics.problem: Rice paddy alternate wetting and drying for methane
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: Flooded rice fields emit methane. Letting them dry at the right moments cuts it without hurting yield.
topics.start: [Oo et al. 2020, DNDC-Rice validation under irrigation practices, Agriculture](https://ideas.repec.org/a/gam/jagris/v10y2020i8p355-d398813.html); [DNDC model](https://www.dndc.sr.unh.edu/)
topics.baseline: Continuous flooding or threshold AWD
topics.angle: DP or RL on a reduced water-balance and methane model, MPC with rainfall forecast

topics.title: Landfill gas collection
topics.problem: Landfill gas wellfield vacuum control
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: Landfills leak methane, a potent greenhouse gas. Tuning the vacuum on each well captures more of it without pulling air into the waste.
topics.start: [Townsend et al. 2005, gas flow model for landfill collection systems, J. Environmental Engineering](https://ascelibrary.com/doi/10.1061/%28ASCE%290733-9372%282005%29131%3A12%281716%29); Darcy-flow model rebuilt
topics.baseline: Monthly manual wellhead tuning
topics.angle: learned well-response model + MPC per well; no public wellhead data

topics.title: Wastewater nitrous oxide
topics.problem: Wastewater N2O mitigation by aeration and recirculation control
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: Treatment plants emit nitrous oxide, a strong greenhouse gas, as a by-product of removing nitrogen. Aeration control can cut it.
topics.start: [Santín et al. 2023, N2O reduction by recirculation control, J. Water Process Engineering](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2023/7cb675cdc712/1_s2.0_S2214714423003215_main.pdf); [bsm2-python](https://bsm2-python.readthedocs.io)
topics.baseline: Ammonia cascade PI
topics.angle: MPC or RL on BSM2 with a learned N2O surrogate

topics.title: Flow battery control
topics.problem: Vanadium redox flow battery: electrolyte flow-rate control
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: Flow batteries store energy in tanks of liquid electrolyte for long durations. Pump too fast and you waste energy; too slow and the cells starve.
topics.start: [Wang et al. 2023, dynamic optimisation of VRFB flow rate, J. Energy Storage](https://research-repository.uwa.edu.au/en/publications/model-based-nonlinear-dynamic-optimisation-for-the-optimal-flow-r/); [Xiong et al. 2023, GRU flow-rate-aware model](https://research.chalmers.se/publication/538370/file/538370_Fulltext.pdf); model rebuilt
topics.baseline: Fixed flow or lookup table
topics.angle: learned dynamics + MPC, open-loop optimal schedule amortized

topics.title: Dynamic line rating
topics.problem: Dynamic line rating in multi-period dispatch
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: Power lines can carry more current when it is cold and windy. Using that headroom lets more renewable power through without building new lines.
topics.start: [Rabecq et al. 2025, dynamic line ratings in AC OPF](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.10832); [NREL hourly DLR data](https://data.openei.org/submissions/6231); [pandapower](https://github.com/e2nIEE/pandapower)
topics.baseline: Static rating
topics.angle: decision-focused line-rating forecasts feeding OPF, MPC with transient conductor temperature

topics.title: Energy-optimal train driving
topics.problem: Energy-optimal train driving under timetable disturbances
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: Pontryagin's principle says how to drive a train: power, cruise, coast, brake. Real timetables and delays turn it into a feedback problem.
topics.start: [Albrecht et al. 2016, key principles of optimal train control, Transportation Research Part B](https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/transb/v94y2016icp482-508.html); [Xie et al. 2023, metro energy under disturbances with RL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.13443)
topics.baseline: The Pontryagin structure (power, hold, coast, brake)
topics.angle: amortize PMP solutions into a policy, RL under delays; trivial unless disturbances are included

topics.title: Electric bus depot charging
topics.problem: Electric bus depot charging scheduling
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: A bus fleet goes electric only if the depot can charge everyone overnight without a huge grid connection. STM's open timetables give a Montreal instance.
topics.start: [Heide et al. 2025, electric bus fleet deployment, World Electric Vehicle Journal](https://www.mdpi.com/2032-6653/16/7/378); [Qi et al. 2025, hierarchical deep RL for bus charging](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10296); [eflips-depot](https://pypi.org/project/eflips-depot); STM GTFS for a Montreal instance
topics.baseline: Plug-and-charge and the ILP
topics.angle: amortize the ILP, MPC with a rolling schedule, RL under uncertainty

topics.title: Truck platooning
topics.problem: Heavy-duty truck platooning: look-ahead energy control
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: Trucks driving close together cut drag. Looking ahead at the hills lets the platoon coordinate speed and save fuel.
topics.start: [Ard et al. 2022, cooperative MPC for truck platooning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.02119); [Besselink et al. 2015, cyber-physical control of road freight](https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.03466)
topics.baseline: Cruise control and CACC
topics.angle: look-ahead MPC over road grade, learned fuel map, policy distilled from MPC

topics.title: Storm-surge barrier closure
topics.problem: Storm-surge barrier closure as optimal stopping (Maeslant, MOSE)
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: Closing a surge barrier stops a flood but halts shipping. The call has to be made on forecasts that are wrong in known ways.
topics.start: [Trace-Kleeberg et al. 2025, Coastal Engineering](https://eprints.soton.ac.uk/502090) (16 years of forecasts vs gauge); [Umgiesser et al. 2021, floods in Venice, NHESS](https://nhess.copernicus.org/articles/21/2679/2021/)
topics.baseline: Threshold rule on the forecast
topics.angle: POMDP or optimal stopping with a learned forecast-error model; false closures vs misses

topics.title: Forecast-informed dam releases
topics.problem: Forecast-informed emergency dam pre-releases
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: Release water before a big storm to make room for the flood, but release too much and the reservoir runs short. Ensemble forecasts make it a decision under uncertainty.
topics.start: [Brodeur et al. 2024, synthetic forecast ensembles for forecast-informed reservoir operations, Water Resources Research](https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10530480)
topics.baseline: Ensemble forecast operations rule with a risk curve
topics.angle: policy over ensemble statistics, decision-focused forecast calibration

topics.title: Drought restrictions
topics.problem: Drought restriction policies for urban water supply
topics.section: Climate: land, methane, storage, transit and adaptation
topics.hook: When should a city ask people to cut water use, and by how much? A stochastic DP question that droughts make urgent.
topics.start: [Eum et al. 2011, sampling stochastic DP with a hedging rule, J. Water Resources Planning and Management](https://ascelibrary.com/doi/10.1061/%28ASCE%29WR.1943-5452.0000095); [Macian-Sorribes et al. 2015, HESS](https://hess.copernicus.org/articles/19/3925/2015/hess-19-3925-2015-metrics.html)
topics.baseline: Fixed trigger rule curves
topics.angle: sampling SDP, policy search over thresholds, learned inflow model

topics.title: Nonlinear 20-story seismic benchmark
topics.problem: Choose active actuator forces or semi-active damper commands at each control step from noisy floor accelerations to reduce inter-story drift and floor accelerations of a 20-story steel frame that yields under strong earthquakes, within the benchmark's device and sensor constraints.
topics.hook: This is the structural control community's standard yardstick, with a fixed nonlinear evaluation model and fixed criteria, so a learned controller is compared with decades of published designs. On a smaller five-story benchmark a model-free RL controller reported about 25% more drift reduction than LQG; testing whether that holds on the yielding 20-story frame is a clean project.
topics.start: [Ohtori, Christenson, Spencer and Dyke, third-generation benchmark control problems for seismically excited nonlinear buildings (3-, 9- and 20-story SAC frames), benchmark definition page](https://sstl.cee.illinois.edu/benchmarks/bench3def/); [NEES database of structural control benchmark problems, MATLAB data and simulation files](https://datacenterhub.org/resources/257); [Spencer 2004, editorial on the benchmark special issue, J. Eng. Mech.](https://ascelibrary.com/doi/10.1061/%28ASCE%290733-9399%282004%29130%3A4%28363%29); [Eshkevari et al. 2021, RL-Controller for active structural control, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.07616)
topics.baseline: the benchmark's sample LQG active controller, plus the uncontrolled frame
topics.angle: RL or learned-model MPC that uses the nonlinear (yielding) evaluation model; amortize the MPC into an output-feedback network and test across records and intensities

topics.title: Wind-excited 76-story tower with ATMD
topics.problem: Choose the active tuned mass damper force on top of a 76-story, 306 m tower from a few floor accelerations to cut wind-induced floor accelerations under wind-tunnel loads, with force within ±118 kN, stroke within 95 cm, and building stiffness uncertain by ±15%.
topics.hook: The building, the wind-tunnel loads and both an LQG and a hard-constrained MPC (±118 kN, 95 cm stroke) are published, so the project is about beating a known controller rather than building a model. The open question is whether a cheap explicit policy keeps the MPC's constraint handling when stiffness is off by 15%.
topics.start: [Mei, Kareem and Kantor 2004, model predictive control of wind-excited building: benchmark study, J. Eng. Mech.](https://nathaz.nd.edu/journals/%282004%29ModelPredictiveControlofWind-ExcitedBuilding.pdf); [Yang, Lin and Jabbari 2004, multiobjective controllers on the same benchmark vs LQG, J. Eng. Mech.](https://ascelibrary.com/doi/10.1061/%28ASCE%290733-9399%282004%29130%3A4%28471%29); [benchmark index, wind-excited 76-story building with MATLAB models](https://sstl.cee.illinois.edu/benchmarks/); [NEES structural control benchmark files](https://datacenterhub.org/resources/257); [wind tunnel data, NEES-2014-1241](https://datacenterhub.org/landingpages/519/519_LandingPage.html)
topics.baseline: the benchmark LQG sample controller and the constrained MPC of Mei et al. (2004)
topics.angle: amortize the constrained MPC into an explicit policy, or train a policy robust to the stiffness range by domain randomization

topics.title: Bridge deck maintenance from NBI ratings
topics.problem: Each year, choose do-nothing, maintain, repair or replace for every deck in a bridge network from noisy condition ratings, to minimize life-cycle cost under an annual budget and a limit on the share of decks in poor condition.
topics.hook: The NBI files give a deck rating for every listed US bridge in each year from 1992 to 2025, so the deterioration model comes from real data. On a Pennsylvania network, a constrained multi-agent DRL policy cost about 32% less than the state DOT's policy and about 6% less than a tuned condition-based policy.
topics.start: [Bhattacharya, Saifullah and Papakonstantinou 2024, DRL-driven life-cycle management of bridge and pavement systems (PennDOT and Hampton Roads networks), IABMAS](https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10552119); [Andriotis and Papakonstantinou 2020, DRL inspection and maintenance planning under incomplete information and constraints, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.01380); [FHWA National Bridge Inventory annual ASCII files 1992-2025 (deck item 58, superstructure 59, substructure 60)](https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/bridge/nbi/ascii.cfm); model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: a condition-based threshold policy tuned on the same model, and the agency's rule-based policy
topics.angle: estimate Markov transitions from NBI deck rating histories; exact constrained DP or POMDP for one deck, multi-agent actor-critic with Lagrangian budget constraints for the network

topics.title: Montreal water main renewal
topics.problem: Choose which street segments' water mains to renew each year under a fixed budget, given break histories and segment condition data with uncertain future break rates, to minimize breaks and repair costs over a multi-year horizon.
topics.hook: Montreal publishes the date and location of water-main repairs back to 1972, plus its own A-D intervention class for each street segment, so a local project can test a model against the city's actual plan. In Syracuse, ranking by past breaks already reached a precision of 0.48 on the riskiest 1% of mains, against 0.62 for a boosted-tree model.
topics.start: [Kumar et al. 2018, using machine learning to assess the risk of and prevent water main breaks (Syracuse), arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.03597); [Ville de Montreal, water-main break repairs from 1972 with coordinates, CC-BY 4.0](https://www.donneesquebec.ca/recherche/fr/dataset/vmtl-reparation-reseau-eau-potable); [Ville de Montreal, intervention plan results by street segment, classes A-D, lengths and costs](https://www.donneesquebec.ca/recherche/fr/dataset/0d5fab8e-f673-48fd-96dd-745f50ca1ec0); repair records carry no pipe ID, so join them spatially to segments; model rebuilt from the paper
topics.baseline: rank segments by past break count (the strongest heuristic in Kumar et al.) or follow the city's A-D intervention classes
topics.angle: decision-focused learning: train the break-rate model on the regret of the budgeted selection (a knapsack) instead of prediction error; extend to a multi-year DP

topics.title: Fatigue inspection planning, offshore wind
topics.problem: Decide when to inspect and when to repair each fatigue-prone component of an offshore wind support structure or k-out-of-n system, with crack size seen only through imperfect inspections, to minimize inspection, repair and system-failure costs.
topics.hook: An inspection is only worth what it changes in the repair decision, and a POMDP belief policy prices exactly that. Morato et al. found POMDP policies substantially cheaper than the heuristic rules used in risk-based inspection, and the environments run on NumPy alone.
topics.start: [Morato et al. 2022, optimal inspection and maintenance planning for deteriorating structural components through dynamic Bayesian networks and MDPs, Structural Safety (arXiv)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.04547); [Leroy et al. 2023, IMP-MARL, environments for infrastructure management planning, arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.11551); [IMP-MARL code: k-out-of-n and offshore wind fatigue environments plus heuristics, Apache-2.0, NumPy only](https://github.com/moratodpg/imp_marl)
topics.baseline: the expert-based heuristic inspection and repair policies shipped with IMP-MARL
topics.angle: exact point-based POMDP on one component, then multi-agent actor-critic on the system; measure the value of information of each inspection

topics.title: Post-storm repair crew dispatch
